purpose: Replace story cutscene illustrations with title-screen quality. Local native export uses deterministic palette conversion, no API calls.

prompts.campus:
Use case: illustration-story. Create ONE finished pixel-art cutscene illustration for the Game Boy Color adventure Negro Matapacos, the transition from rescued students on Alameda to the university campus.
Reference image: the provided title illustration is the definitive reference for DOG IDENTITY, pixel-art craftsmanship, palette and layered Santiago atmosphere. Match its quality. This is a new scene, not a copy of the title layout.
Composition: wide landscape 3:2 illustration, designed to be reduced to 160x104 pixels. Frame the hero prominently on the LEFT as a large, beautifully shaded three-quarter bust (ears to chest about 85 native pixels tall), looking RIGHT toward a rescued university student and the campus. Black Chilean street dog, one upright natural ear and one folded ear, long real canine muzzle, amber eye, gray-blue highlights defining short black fur, expressive hopeful face, vivid red bandana with detailed folds and a tied knot. Retain the title reference's dog proportions, rounded anatomy, strong silhouette and subtle fur texture.
Scene: Santiago university courtyard at golden sunset. On the right a friendly student with dark hair, warm skin, dark clothing and red neck scarf crouches beside him, holding one hand reassuringly near his shoulder and pointing toward the campus entrance. A detailed warm ochre university facade with masonry, roof cornice, tall windows and a visible open arch leads into the next stage. Distant teal Santiago roof silhouettes and Andes, a few students together safely in the courtyard, a small correctly patterned Chilean flag (blue canton and white star, white upper stripe, red lower stripe).
Art: premium lovingly crafted late-1990s handheld pixel illustration, exactly like the supplied title: deliberate crisp square pixel clusters, subtle edge lighting, material shading, layered depth, atmospheric warm cream sky, peach sunset clouds, ochre stone, deep navy ink shadows, muted teal city, saturated red bandana. Art should read at native tiny size. Use rich meaningful texture and a few large simple forms; do not create tiny noisy stippling. Flat blocky schematic faces, stick figures, triangular fox ears, generic icon silhouettes, vector art, blur, antialiasing, photographic texture and 3D rendering are unacceptable.
Layout: fill the entire canvas with the illustration, all important faces and the campus arch in the upper 90 percent. No text, no lettering, no speech bubble, no title, no HUD, no borders, no signatures or watermarks. UI and localized speech will be rendered by the actual game.
prompts.plaza:
Use case: illustration-story. Create ONE finished pixel-art narrative cutscene illustration for Negro Matapacos, the transition from the university rescue to Plaza de la Dignidad in Santiago.
Reference image: the supplied title image is the definitive DOG IDENTITY and art-quality reference. Follow that black dog's natural proportions, one upright and one folded ear, gray-blue short-fur highlights, expressive amber eye and richly folded vivid red bandana. Create a fresh scene in this exact detailed warm pixel-art style.
Composition: wide landscape 3:2, designed to remain beautiful when reduced to 160x104 pixels. A dramatic hopeful low-angle shot of the dog in the LEFT foreground, head raised looking toward the plaza to the RIGHT. He is large and dominant, head and chest about 80 native pixels high, with beautifully shaded dark fur, rounded real canine muzzle, bright eye and saturated red bandana knot fluttering in a breeze. A young student with dark clothes and warm skin stands beside him, looking ahead. On the right a LARGE waving Chilean flag, accurately blue square canton with a single white star, white upper stripe and red lower stripe, held by another student who is mostly behind the flag.
Scenery: Plaza de la Dignidad with an equestrian monument in the middle distance, weathered stone plinth, teal trees, welcoming groups of safely reunited student silhouettes, Santiago architecture and distant peach Andes beneath warm gold sunset clouds. Foreground flags and characters have strong color and shadow; distant buildings and mountain layers have atmospheric depth.
Craftsmanship: premium 1990s handheld pixel-art illustration, match the title's intentional sharp square pixel clusters, layered fur texture, cloth folds, stone texture, edge lighting and convincing architecture. Deep navy shadows, steel-gray fur highlights, cream-peach sky, muted teal city and saturated Chilean red/white/blue. At native 160x104 reduce visual clutter, use larger legible forms and detailed shading, not tiny noisy stippling. Do not make a fox, triangular geometric dog, stick figures, flat color icons, vector art, photorealism, blur, antialiasing or 3D art.
Output: one artwork fills the entire canvas. Keep important faces, monument and flag in the upper 90 percent. Absolutely NO letters, words, titles, labels, UI, frames, watermarks or speech bubbles; dialogue will be drawn in the game.
prompts.mapocho:
Use case: illustration-story. Create ONE finished pixel-art narrative cutscene for Negro Matapacos, the transition from Plaza de la Dignidad toward Río Mapocho.
Reference image: supplied title artwork is the definitive character and craftsmanship reference. The dog must be the same black Chilean street dog, one upright and one folded ear, gray-blue fur highlights, amber eye, natural canine muzzle, detailed vivid red bandana with tied knot.
Composition: wide landscape 3:2 illustration, designed for a 160x104 pixel Game Boy Color cutscene. A cinematic SIDE VIEW of a rescued student and Matapacos running together toward the RIGHT along a Mapocho riverside walkway. Bring the dog close to the viewer in the lower-left/center: a LARGE full-body athletic dog about two-thirds of the canvas width, head raised alertly, legs in a believable running stride, bandana fluttering; layered fur highlights and muscle forms. A young student with dark hair, warm skin, black hooded jacket and red scarf runs just behind him, upper body visible and bent arm gesturing forward. Use a tight composition with their faces large enough to read at small resolution. They are companions heading to safety, not attackers.
Scenery: the Mapocho's recognizable deep CONCRETE river channel through central Santiago, shallow blue-green/brown water beneath the walkway, tall worn embankment walls, an elegant old steel-and-stone bridge over the channel in the right middle distance. Bridge arches and railings clearly visible; channel recedes toward layered Santiago rooftops, trees and peach Andes. A tiny distant police silhouette with a capture net near the bridge hints at the next encounter, but main focus is dog and student. Warm cream-gold evening sky and orange clouds, teal city shadows, ochre concrete, stone textures, directional sunset edge light.
Art: match the supplied title's premium detailed 1990s pixel-art quality. Deliberate crisp square pixel clusters, convincing canine anatomy and cloth folds, shaded architectural detail and strong foreground/background depth. Deep navy shadows, gray-blue fur lights, muted teal city, cream/peach sky and saturated red bandana. A few large readable forms with purposeful texture; avoid noisy stippling. No schematic rectangles, stick figures, geometric fox, flat vector icons, blur, smooth antialiasing, photography or 3D rendering.
Output: artwork fills entire canvas. Keep all important faces, dog's bandana and bridge in upper 90 percent. No text, lettering, speech bubbles, UI, frames, titles, watermarks or signatures; bilingual dialogue will be added by the game.
prompts.moneda:
Use case: illustration-story. Create ONE finished pixel-art narrative cutscene for Negro Matapacos, the transition from the Mapocho rescue to the final showdown at Palacio de La Moneda.
Reference: supplied title illustration establishes exact hero identity and premium pixel craftsmanship. Keep the same natural black Chilean street dog, one upright ear and one folded ear, amber eye, long rounded gray-blue shaded muzzle, expressive short black fur and vivid red bandana with folded fabric and tied knot.
Composition: wide landscape 3:2, designed to read as a 160x104 Game Boy Color cutscene. The hero stands in the LEFT foreground in an alert three-quarter pose, face and chest large and carefully shaded (head to chest about 75 native pixels tall), looking RIGHT. Beside him a rescued dark-haired student in dark clothes and a red scarf points urgently toward La Moneda. Faces and bandana should be large enough to read when tiny. In the RIGHT middle foreground, clearly show a GREEN ARMORED WATER-CANNON TRUCK (Chilean guanaco): squat angular body, dark wheels, armored windshield, green panels, roof-mounted water cannon turned left. It is parked and NOT spraying now, showing the coming danger. It should be distinct and unmistakable at native scale, not hidden behind characters.
Scenery: La Moneda's recognizable broad pale cream neoclassical facade in the middle distance: two stories, repeated tall window bays, stone details, restrained cornice, central dark entrance arch, a correct Chilean flag above (blue canton with white star, white upper stripe and red lower stripe). Paved forecourt leading to palace. Atmospheric teal Santiago rooftops and peach Andes under a warm cream-gold sunset. Foreground hero has deep rich dark shades and vivid red fabric; the palace is bright and inviting beyond the vehicle.
Style: match the title's deliberate crisp pixel clusters, rich but legible fur texture, metal highlights, cloth folds, masonry and atmospheric depth. Hand-crafted premium 1990s pixel art, deep navy shadows, steel-gray canine highlights, cream/peach sky, teal urban layers, stone gold, olive green armor. Avoid noisy tiny stippling. NO simplified geometric fox, stick figures, rectangular placeholder buildings, flat-color icon art, vector look, blur, smooth antialiasing, photography or 3D render.
Output one finished artwork filling the canvas, important faces and palace and vehicle in upper 90 percent. NO text, letters, signage, dialogue boxes, UI, titles, borders, watermarks or signatures. The actual game adds bilingual speech and UI.
